event.name: 8 June 2008 Northwest Peloponnese (Andravida/Movri) earthquake
event.tectonic_setting: NW Peloponnese, western Greece; reactivated deeply buried NE-SW striking fault zone near the Hellenic arc

reference.title: Rupture Process and Aftershocks Relocation of the 8 June 2008 Mw 6.4 Earthquake in Northwest Peloponnese, Western Greece
reference.journal: Bulletin of the Seismological Society of America

inversion.method: Parallel nonnegative least-squares finite-fault inversion using multiple time windows; 3 x 3 km subfaults on a 66 x 42 km plane; 24 overlapping time windows (2 s each, 1 s overlap); moment minimization and edge damping.
inversion.green_function_model: Frequency-wavenumber synthetics with the regional 1D velocity models used in the study; observed and synthetic waveforms bandpass filtered at 0.05-0.125 Hz.
inversion.notes: FIGURE-DIGITIZED ESTIMATE, NOT THE ORIGINAL INVERSION SUBFAULT ARRAY. Slip is reconstructed from grayscale Figure 8 (page 3384) of the uploaded article, in cm on the published 0-150 cm nonlinear grayscale bar, then reported here in meters to 0.01 m increments. The plotted open circles are relocated aftershocks, the star is the relocated mainshock, the thin dark lines are plot grid lines, and white contours with black numerals (20, 40 and 80) represent slip isolines; NONE of these marks are treated as slip observations. Digitization masks obvious gridlines, numeric contour labels, the hypocenter star and identified dark aftershock speckles, closes narrow white contour breaks, performs spatial smoothing and conservatively suppresses suspicious amplitude in three aftershock-rich regions. Suppression may underestimate genuine slip near the aftershock clusters; areas behind text and closely spaced markers cannot be recovered uniquely. No color version or machine-readable original patch slip array was used. Values are figure-derived approximation and are NOT independently inverted subfault slips. The authors report an approximate 150 cm peak around 7-20 km depth in the NE and a weaker 20-50 cm SW patch, with two deeper patches near 25-30 km. The 22 x 14 digitized grid has a largest cell 1.28 m, below the paper's ~1.50 m local figure peak, as expected for smoothing and 3-km sampling; its grid-wide mean is 0.098 m and must not be read as paper-reported mean slip. Fault strike/dip/rake (210/86/162 degrees) are an approximate NE-SW nodal-plane proxy based on the CMT alternative to the 301/72/4 mechanism listed in Table 3, NOT a precise preferred 3D segment geometry explicitly specified by this paper. The along-strike index increases from the NE (higher labelled latitude, left of plot) to SW (lower latitude, right of plot). Approximate per-column latitude is read from the plot labels (38.2 to ~37.75 deg); patch longitude is null because the cross section alone does not georeference 2D positions. Depths are nominal down-dip-center depths for an assumed top edge at 0 km and 86 degree dip; the chart plots depth to 40 km but the parameterized down-dip width is 42 km. Neither a true 3D upper edge nor individual patch depths are specified in the paper. Origin seconds :28 follow an independent EMSC catalog; the article itself gives origin time to minute precision (12:25 GMT); the study-specific relocated mainshock hypocenter is 37.924 N, 21.46 E, 18 km. The paper seismic moment 0.449 x 10^26 dyne-cm corresponds to 4.49 x 10^18 N m, and is the inversion constraint, not an integral calculated from this approximate image-digitized mesh. Original detailed faulting_style description: right-lateral strike-slip.

provenance.compiled_by: Figure 8 grayscale digitization from user-provided Konstantinou et al. (2009) PDF and plot image; aftershock-overlay suppression and contour-aware filtering
